items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: It said that you used to cut school to go watch Elvis Presley movies. Loved him.

ctx.x: Very great jazz bass player. He grew up in Philadelphia and he actually wrote "Money Money, Money." He did that bass line with Gamble & Huff. If you go back, I'll bet he made more money from that song than he made from anything in his entire life. Gamble & Huff gave him a piece of the song, because he came up with that [scats] — whatever it was, I can't remember it and I can't sing it exactly. But one morning I came in to the studio and he was there and I hear [scats]. He was practicing the first Bach suite. This…
That's great. This has really been a fascinating chat. And I wanted to ask you two things that I read and we'll wrap it up. It said that you used to cut school to go watch Elvis Presley movies.

Loved him. Learned how to play the guitar as a kid, a real kid dirt young. And I learned how to — my mother used to say in that rough neighborhood where we grew up, she used to say, "You could go into a bar and probably make more money than I made in the store today."
